data.message:
Review the claims of profile R1008.
It is about: researcher Krisztina Kiss (R1008).

Claims:
1. Long-range dependence and periodicity characterisation of industrial Ethernet traffic in Modbus and EtherNet/IP networks. [SYN-PUB-10474]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-10474] publication · Characterising Normal Behaviour in Industrial Ethernet Networks: A Long-Term Measurement Study · 2013 · researchers R1008
Characterising Normal Behaviour in Industrial Ethernet Networks: A Long-Term Measurement Study (2013, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics).
Authors: Goran Milošević (outside co-author); Marko Đorđević (outside co-author); Reinhilde Mayer (outside co-author); Krisztina Kiss (R1008).
Keywords: traffic characterisation; industrial Ethernet; long-range dependence; measurement study; Hurst parameter.
This measurement study presents a 12-month passive capture of traffic from four industrial sites—two discrete manufacturing lines, one water utility, and one district heating plant—totalling approximately 680 GB of raw packet data. The study characterises normal traffic behaviour through 22 statistical descriptors per flow, including coefficient of variation of inter-packet gaps, entropy of destination port distributions, and autocorrelation structure of payload-length time series. Results show that industrial Ethernet traffic exhibits strong periodicity at scales of seconds to hours, with Hurst parameter estimates between 0.61 and 0.79 across sites, indicating long-range dependence. The study documents characteristic differences between Modbus, EtherNet/IP, and proprietary vendor protocols and quantifies seasonal variation. The dataset and feature extraction code are described in sufficient detail to support reproducibility. Findings inform design choices for unsupervised detectors and highlight risks of training on short captures.

Review the claims of profile R1015.
It is about: researcher Vuk Đukić (R1015).

Claims:
1. Anomaly detection on Modbus protocol traffic using unsupervised learning trained on benign communications. [SYN-PUB-10523]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-10523] publication · Unsupervised anomaly detection on Modbus traffic · 2024 · researchers R1015
Unsupervised anomaly detection on Modbus traffic (2024, journal, Journal of Industrial Security).
Authors: Vuk Đukić (R1015); Milena Ostojić (outside co-author); Dragan Kovač (outside co-author).
Industrial control systems increasingly rely on Modbus, a legacy serial communication protocol widely deployed in manufacturing and critical infrastructure environments. Despite its prevalence, Modbus lacks built-in security mechanisms, making it highly susceptible to network-based attacks. This paper presents an unsupervised anomaly detection framework specifically designed for Modbus traffic analysis. The proposed approach leverages autoencoder-based neural networks trained exclusively on benign traffic to establish a baseline behavioural profile of legitimate industrial communications. Anomalies are identified by measuring reconstruction error against learned normal patterns, without requiring labelled attack data. The framework is evaluated on a synthetic dataset generated from a real-world programmable logic controller testbed, covering scenarios such as unauthorised function code injection, coil manipulation, and replay attacks. Experimental results demonstrate detection rates exceeding 94% across all attack categories, with a false positive rate below 2%. The paper also analyses the impact of traffic window size and encoding granularity on detection performance, offering practical guidance for deployment in resource-constrained industrial environments.

Kalman-filter-based plausibility checking for soil temperature sensor arrays with heterogeneous failure modes (2024, journal, Measurement Science and Sensor Diagnostics).
Authors: Tijana Ostojić (outside co-author); Dragana Vukić (outside co-author); Jana Novotná (outside co-author); Vladan Nedić (R0060); Žarko Ivanović (R0630); Žarko Jakovljević (R0754).
Keywords: Kalman filter; soil temperature; sensor fault isolation; heat diffusion model; edge computation.
Soil temperature arrays deployed at multiple depths are subject to at least four distinct failure modes: complete open-circuit failure, partial short inducing constant-low readings, slow drift from burial-induced mechanical stress on thermistor leads, and intermittent noise injection from nearby electric fence controllers. This paper applies an ensemble Kalman filter to a seven-sensor vertical array, using a one-dimensional heat diffusion model as the process model parameterised with local soil thermal diffusivity estimates. The filter's innovation sequence is monitored with a chi-squared test to isolate faulty sensors without discarding the ensemble. In a 14-month field deployment at two sites in the Banat region, the method identified all 9 sensor faults confirmed by physical inspection, correctly attributed failure mode in 7 of those cases, and continued providing usable profile estimates from the remaining functional sensors throughout each fault episode. [SYN-PUB-03570] publication · Certificate-Based Firmware Authentication for Resource-Constrained Devices Without Persistent Internet Connectivity · 2022 · researchers R0286
Certificate-Based Firmware Authentication for Resource-Constrained Devices Without Persistent Internet Connectivity (2022, journal, IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing).
Authors: Kateřina Horáčková (outside co-author); Lena Svensson (outside co-author); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Ана Рајић (R0286).
Keywords: X.509; offline certificate validation; firmware authentication; constrained devices; public key infrastructure.
Public-key certificate validation normally depends on online revocation checking, which is infeasible for industrial field devices that communicate only intermittently. This paper proposes an offline certificate validation scheme for firmware authentication in which short-lived leaf certificates, valid for a configurable window of 24–168 hours, are bundled with the firmware image and verified against a pre-installed intermediate CA certificate stored in device ROM. Certificate revocation is handled by expiry rather than CRL or OCSP. The scheme uses X.509 profiles trimmed to fit within 512 bytes using a custom DER subset. Implementation and evaluation were performed on an ARM Cortex-M3 device with 32 KB RAM; certificate parsing and verification completed in 310 ms using a software ECC library. Claims:

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-03570] publication · Certificate-Based Firmware Authentication for Resource-Constrained Devices Without Persistent Internet Connectivity · 2022 · researchers R0286
Certificate-Based Firmware Authentication for Resource-Constrained Devices Without Persistent Internet Connectivity (2022, journal, IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing).
Authors: Kateřina Horáčková (outside co-author); Lena Svensson (outside co-author); Miroslav Vukić (outside co-author); Ана Рајић (R0286).
Keywords: X.509; offline certificate validation; firmware authentication; constrained devices; public key infrastructure.
Public-key certificate validation normally depends on online revocation checking, which is infeasible for industrial field devices that communicate only intermittently. This paper proposes an offline certificate validation scheme for firmware authentication in which short-lived leaf certificates, valid for a configurable window of 24–168 hours, are bundled with the firmware image and verified against a pre-installed intermediate CA certificate stored in device ROM. Certificate revocation is handled by expiry rather than CRL or OCSP. The scheme uses X.509 profiles trimmed to fit within 512 bytes using a custom DER subset. Implementation and evaluation were performed on an ARM Cortex-M3 device with 32 KB RAM; certificate parsing and verification completed in 310 ms using a software ECC library. The paper analyses the security implications of the short-lived certificate approach under various attacker models, including the case where the attacker can delay delivery to extend a certificate's apparent validity.

Review the claims of pair C001-CH1:R1015.
It is about: researcher Vuk Đukić (R1015) and company ArmaturaSec d.o.o. (C001), challenge C001-CH1.

Claims:
1. C001-CH1 requires a method that can be explained to a plant manager in plain language (C001-CH1). [C001-CH1]

Sources:
[C001-CH1] challenge · We need to detect unusual behaviour on Modbus and BACnet networks without labelled attack data — our clients have never been breached (or don't know it), so we have zero examples of malicious traffic and supervised classifiers are useless to us. · company C001
We need to detect unusual behaviour on Modbus and BACnet networks without labelled attack data — our clients have never been breached (or don't know it), so we have zero examples of malicious traffic and supervised classifiers are useless to us.

Our ProtoSense module watches Modbus and BACnet traffic and is supposed to flag anything that looks wrong. The problem is that none of our clients has ever given us a packet capture that contains a confirmed attack. A few of them have been running their networks for twenty years with no security monitoring at all, so if they were compromised they would not know. We have plenty of normal traffic — we have collected several terabytes of captures from consenting clients over the past three years — but we have nothing labelled as malicious. We tried building a supervised classifier once, fed it data from public ICS datasets, and it flagged so many false positives in real deployments that clients started switching the alerts off. What we actually need is something that learns what normal looks like on a specific site and raises a flag when behaviour drifts from that baseline. We have the traffic archives, we have the hardware to run inference on-device, and we have one engineer who has been reading about anomaly detection for six months. We need a method that works with no attack examples and that we can explain to a plant manager in plain language.

Review the claims of pair C001-CH4:R0233.
It is about: researcher Valentina Stojanović (R0233) and company ArmaturaSec d.o.o. (C001), challenge C001-CH4.

Claims:
1. ArmaturaSec needs automated test skeleton generation triggered by feature additions, working within the existing Python test runner and physical hardware bench (C001-CH4). [C001-CH4]
2. Stojanović co-authored work on model-based test generation from finite automata and statecharts with integration to hardware-in-the-loop execution on microcontroller platforms (SYN-PUB-02949, SYN-PUB-02947, SYN-PUB-02945). [SYN-PUB-02949, SYN-PUB-02947, SYN-PUB-02945]
3. Stojanović co-authored work on model-to-text generation for PLC software with incremental code regeneration when configuration changes occur (SYN-PUB-02958). [SYN-PUB-02958]
4. Stojanović co-authored work on test case generation from model and specification gaps using large language models to extend formal models, which addresses the brittleness failure of the prior spec-driven approach (SYN-PUB-02955). [SYN-PUB-02955]
5. Stojanović conducted a two-year action research collaboration with a Serbian industrial electronics firm producing programmable logic controllers, introducing formal specification practices into their firmware development workflow (SYN-PUB-02952). [SYN-PUB-02952]
6. Stojanović led the FRMTEST project as principal investigator developing a regression testing toolchain for embedded firmware, resulting in a publicly released open-source toolchain (SYN-PRJ-0517). [SYN-PRJ-0517]
7. Together, Stojanović and ArmaturaSec would design a change-triggered test skeleton generator for PLC firmware: when a feature is added, a model-based tool derived from finite automata or LLM-extended formal models produces a Python test skeleton that a junior engineer completes on the existing hardware bench, addressing the stale-test and time-cost problems (C001-CH4, SYN-PUB-02949, SYN-PUB-02958, SYN-PUB-02955, SYN-PUB-02954). Review the claims of profile R0800.
It is about: researcher Tihomir Urošević (R0800).

Claims:
1. Path-loss modelling and link-budget prediction for indoor and industrial environments using empirical measurement data and deterministic tools. [SYN-PUB-08743, SYN-PUB-08739, SYN-PUB-06790]
2. Wideband channel characterisation and delay-spread measurement in industrial and warehouse environments using vector network analysers and channel sounding. [SYN-PUB-08740, SYN-PRJ-0351]
3. Propagation through building materials at sub-GHz frequencies, including penetration loss of greenhouse structures and spatial correlation of signal strength in hospital buildings. [SYN-PUB-06790, SYN-PUB-08744]
4. Reverberation chamber measurement of antenna radiation efficiency and performance characterisation for IoT devices. [SYN-PUB-08742]
5. LoRaWAN network planning, gateway placement optimisation, and coverage prediction in mixed indoor-outdoor industrial sites. [SYN-PUB-08743, SYN-PRJ-0350]
6. Angle-of-arrival estimation for indoor localisation using switched-beam antenna arrays and received signal strength differences. [SYN-PUB-08745]
7. Open to contract research for propagation measurement campaigns and link-budget studies, with equipment access to reverberation chamber, vector network analyser, and software-defined radio channel sounder. [R0800]

Review the claims of proposal C003-CH1-R0365.
It is about: researcher Bojan Erić (R0365) and company AutomVoj a.d. (C003), challenge C003-CH1.

Claims:
1. AutomVoj a.d. works in robotics and industrial automation. [C003]
2. Bojan Erić is an Associate Professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering (Machine Design and Mechanics), Faculty of Technical Sciences. [R0365]
3. Welded mild steel conveyor frames are cracking at the main crossmember-to-stringer connections after approximately 18 months of chilled operation at 2–6 °C, but the same frames pass load testing at room temperature in the workshop. [C003-CH1]
4. AutomVoj has replaced 14 frame assemblies under warranty this year; two failed sections remain in storage with site-visit photos and measurements. [C003-CH1]
5. The company suspects thermal cycling, condensation, and vibration are interacting to cause the failure, but cannot reproduce or characterise the phenomenon at ambient workshop conditions. [C003-CH1]
6. The workshop does not have equipment or know-how for low-temperature cyclic load testing. [C003-CH1]
7. A 2023 study reports that welding residual stress roughly doubles the effective crack driving force in welded joints and reduces fatigue life by approximately half compared with analyses that neglect it. [W4388490665]
8. Two failed frame assemblies in storage, with site-visit photos and field measurements, available as primary specimens for analysis. [C003-CH1]

[SYN-PRJ-0011] project · VISIONQC: AI quality control for SMEs · 2023 · researchers R0548
VISIONQC: AI quality control for SMEs (Innovation Fund, 2023–2025).
Participants: R0548 academic partner.
VISIONQC aims to bring AI-powered quality control capabilities within reach of small and medium enterprises that lack the data infrastructure and machine learning expertise of large manufacturers. The project develops a modular inspection platform combining few-shot defect detection, synthetic data augmentation, and edge-deployable quantized models, enabling SMEs to configure reliable inspection pipelines with minimal labeled data and without cloud dependency. As academic partner, Stojanović leads algorithm development and validation, ensuring that research outputs are translated into production-ready components. Pilot deployments are conducted at two regional manufacturing SMEs producing metal and polymer components, with key performance indicators targeting detection accuracy above 90% and setup time under two working days per new product type. The project runs from 2023 to 2025 under the Innovation Fund (synthetic) program.

Review the claims of profile R0800.
It is about: researcher Tihomir Urošević (R0800).

Claims:
1. Led work package on propagation modelling and link-budget validation in AGRILINK (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia), a LoRaWAN project for smart greenhouse monitoring with agricultural partners. [SYN-PRJ-0350]

Sources:
[SYN-PRJ-0350] project · Low-Power Wide-Area Connectivity for Smart Greenhouse Monitoring in the Pannonian Region · 2022 · researchers R0800
AGRILINK: Low-Power Wide-Area Connectivity for Smart Greenhouse Monitoring in the Pannonian Region (Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia, 2022–2025).
Participants: R0800 work package leader.
Partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad; University of Szeged, Faculty of Engineering, Hungary; Agro-Innovation Centre Palić (fictional); Greentech Pannonia d.o.o. (fictional).
AGRILINK develops and validates a LoRaWAN-based sensor network architecture for monitoring temperature, humidity, CO₂, and soil moisture in greenhouse clusters across northern Serbia and southern Hungary. The University of Novi Sad component is responsible for radio propagation characterisation of greenhouse structures, network planning methodology, and gateway placement optimisation. Tihomir Urošević leads the work package on propagation modelling and link-budget validation, coordinating measurement campaigns at partner greenhouse sites. The project also produces an open-access planning guide for small agricultural producers considering IoT adoption, and delivers a pilot deployment covering approximately 3 hectares of greenhouse area near Subotica.

Review the claims of proposal C003-CH1-R0365.
It is about: researcher Bojan Erić (R0365) and company AutomVoj a.d. (C003), challenge C003-CH1.

Claims:
1. A 2023 study reports that welding residual stress significantly increases the effective crack driving force and reduces fatigue life, with the fatigue life at the weld toe without considering residual stress being approximately twice that when residual stress is considered. [W4388490665]
2. AutoCAD Mechanical drawings for conveyor layout and structural design, together with in-house MIG/MAG welded mild steel hollow-section frame fabrication. [C003, C003/website/2024-01-15/What We Do — Conveyor and Sorting Systems for Food and Beverage Producers]
3. An engineering team of 212 engineers, electricians, and technicians available to support the project. [C003]
4. Fabrication shop, electrical assembly area, and in-house testing floor all under one roof on the Zrenjanin site. [C003]
5. Erić co-authored work on fracture toughness of weld HAZ microstructures at temperatures down to −60 °C using Charpy impact and CTOD testing. [SYN-PUB-04476]
6. Erić co-authored work on residual stress measurement by X-ray diffraction and FE simulation of residual stress redistribution under cyclic loading in welds and in welded box sections. [SYN-PUB-04478, SYN-PUB-04481]
7. Erić co-authored publications covering low-temperature fracture toughness of weld HAZ microstructures down to −60 °C and thermo-mechanical fatigue with DIC crack monitoring. [SYN-PUB-04476, SYN-PUB-04482, SYN-PUB-04475]

Review the free text of proposal C003-CH1-R0365.
It is about: researcher Bojan Erić (R0365) and company AutomVoj a.d. (C003), challenge C003-CH1.

The claims are checked one by one elsewhere: take them as given. In the proposal each one shows as ⟨claim N⟩.
Check only the other text: the research questions, approach, plan, first steps, the reasoning under "Why this pair" and
the terms agreed up front.

Free text may propose new work and new data ("collect", "label", "set up", "measure", "aim for"), and may reason from the
claims. List a sentence only when it:
- presents as already true a fact about the company or the researcher (data, recordings, a dataset size, history,
  equipment, staff, a skill, what a method does, a past result) that neither the claims nor the sources state;
- works on data the company is not shown to have: for every archive, dataset, log, set of past scans or recordings the
  plan uses as existing, find the claim or source that says the company has it, with the properties the text gives it
  (size, period, format, the device it comes from, its labels). Data the plan says it will collect is fine;
- says what a side lacks or cannot do, and the claims and sources do not say so, or say the opposite;
- contradicts a claim or a source;
- plans work that breaks a limit the company states (a rate it may not go below, hardware it cannot change).
Quote each such sentence whole, exactly as written. Give one reason per sentence and name the claim or source it rests on.
Return an empty list when the free text is fine.

Review the claims of pair C008-CH1:R0800.
It is about: researcher Tihomir Urošević (R0800) and company Elekron Sistemi a.d. (C008), challenge C008-CH1.

Claims:
1. Urošević led a work package on propagation modelling and link-budget validation in AGRILINK, a LoRaWAN project with agricultural and university partners (SYN-PRJ-0350). [SYN-PRJ-0350]
2. Urošević and Elekron Sistemi would conduct link-budget measurements in the basement meter rooms to identify path-loss contributions and evaluate compact sub-GHz antenna options that recover signal margin without replacing gateways, within LoRaWAN duty-cycle limits (C008-CH1, SYN-PUB-08743, SYN-PUB-06790, SYN-PUB-08741). [C008-CH1, SYN-PUB-08743, SYN-PUB-06790, SYN-PUB-08741]
3. SYN-PUB-08743 covers link-budget prediction and SYN-PUB-08741 covers compact antenna design; neither record covers adaptive spreading-factor control or packet-recovery algorithms. [SYN-PUB-08743, SYN-PUB-08741]
4. The 14-month project duration and fixed-price municipal contracts with three clients in Bosnia and North Macedonia constrain time available for field validation (C008-CH1, C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Receives Provincial Innovation Fund Grant for LoRaWAN Signal Research). [C008-CH1, C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Receives Provincial Innovation Fund Grant for LoRaWAN Signal Research]

Sources:

Review the claims of pair C008-CH2:R0548.
It is about: researcher Nikola Stojanović (R0548) and company Elekron Sistemi a.d. (C008), challenge C008-CH2.

Claims:
1. As academic partner in the VISIONQC project, Stojanović leads algorithm development and validation to translate research outputs into production-ready inspection components for SMEs. [SYN-PRJ-0011]
2. SYN-PUB-06396 validates methods with two industrial partners producing metal stampings and injection-moulded plastic components; weld-spatter texture on powder-coat-ready sheet steel may require additional domain adaptation work not covered by those records. [SYN-PUB-06396]
3. SYN-PUB-06389 covers quantization and pruning for edge deployment; the VISIONQC project record describes development and validation of a modular inspection platform for SMEs but does not describe deployment in a two-shift continuous production setting. [SYN-PUB-06389, SYN-PRJ-0011]

Sources:
[SYN-PRJ-0011] project · VISIONQC: AI quality control for SMEs · 2023 · researchers R0548
VISIONQC: AI quality control for SMEs (Innovation Fund, 2023–2025).
Participants: R0548 academic partner.
VISIONQC aims to bring AI-powered quality control capabilities within reach of small and medium enterprises that lack the data infrastructure and machine learning expertise of large manufacturers. The project develops a modular inspection platform combining few-shot defect detection, synthetic data augmentation, and edge-deployable quantized models, enabling SMEs to configure reliable inspection pipelines with minimal labeled data and without cloud dependency. As academic partner, Stojanović leads algorithm development and validation, ensuring that research outputs are translated into production-ready components. Pilot deployments are conducted at two regional manufacturing SMEs producing metal and polymer components, with key performance indicators targeting detection accuracy above 90% and setup time under two working days per new product type. Our quality assurance team writes regression tests by hand for every firmware release; with four hardware variants and monthly release cycles that's eating about 35% of total engineering time and we're still shipping bugs that automated tests should catch.

We release firmware roughly once a month across four hardware variants: the original NetGuard-OT board, the Mini, and two older boards we still maintain for clients under long-term support contracts. Before each release our QA team runs a regression suite that they have been building by hand since 2015. The suite now has around 1,400 test cases. Writing new cases for a feature, updating old ones when hardware behaviour changes, and running everything on four boards takes about two and a half weeks of engineering time per cycle. That is the 35% figure. We have also shipped three bugs in the past year that the regression suite should have caught but did not because the relevant test cases were out of date. We have tried generating tests from our internal protocol specifications but the tooling we built for that was brittle and the team abandoned it. Review the claims of pair C008-CH2:R0593.
It is about: researcher Đuro Simić (R0593) and company Elekron Sistemi a.d. (C008), challenge C008-CH2.

Claims:
1. Simić co-authored a publication on shielding gas composition effects on spatter and bead geometry in MIG welding of thin sheet. [SYN-PUB-06842]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-06842] publication · Shielding Gas Composition Effects on Weld Bead Geometry and Spatter in MIG Welding of 1.0 mm DC01 Sheet at Low Heat Input · 2023 · researchers R0593
Shielding Gas Composition Effects on Weld Bead Geometry and Spatter in MIG Welding of 1.0 mm DC01 Sheet at Low Heat Input (2023, journal, International Journal of Welding Science and Practice).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593); Tamara Novković (outside co-author); Uroš Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: shielding gas; Ar/CO₂; thin sheet; heat input; bead geometry.
Very thin mild-steel sheet (1.0 mm DC01) presents a narrow operating window in MIG welding because heat input must be minimised to avoid burn-through while maintaining fusion. This paper reports the effect of Ar/CO₂ mixture ratios (75/25, 82/18, 90/10, and 97/3 vol%) on spatter mass, bead width, dilution, and distortion in bead-on-plate welds at a fixed heat input of 85 J/mm. Forty-eight specimens were welded and measured. Ar/CO₂ 90/10 produced the lowest spatter mass (0.06 g/m) and the most consistent bead width (coefficient of variation 4.2 %), while 75/25 produced 0.21 g/m spatter. Hardness traverses across the heat-affected zone showed a maximum of 198 HV1 for all gas compositions, indicating no detrimental microstructural change. Distortion, measured by three-point deflection, was lowest at 97/3 but accompanied by an irregular bead profile with 14 % of runs showing incomplete fusion. The 90/10 ratio is recommended as the practical optimum for this thickness.

Active learning with model uncertainty sampling for efficient annotation in industrial inspection pipelines (2021, journal, International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology).
Authors: Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Dragana Ilić (outside co-author); Gregor Vesel (outside co-author).
Keywords: active learning; annotation efficiency; defect detection; model uncertainty; industrial inspection.
Labeling defect images in industrial settings is expensive and requires domain expertise, making the efficient allocation of annotation effort a critical practical concern. This paper proposes an active learning framework for industrial defect detection that uses ensemble-based model uncertainty to prioritize the most informative unlabeled samples for expert annotation. A Monte Carlo dropout ensemble estimates epistemic uncertainty at the instance and region levels, and a diversity-aware sampling strategy prevents the selection of redundant near-duplicate crops from the same production batch. The framework is integrated into a realistic annotation pipeline validated with two industrial partners producing metal stampings and injection-molded plastic components. Across both domains, the active learning approach achieves 90% of fully supervised baseline performance using only 35% of the total available labeled data, reducing annotation cost by an estimated 58% in practitioner time. Small Planar Inverted-F Antenna for 868 MHz LoRa End-Node Integration (2016, journal, Microwave and Optical Technology Letters (European Edition)).
Authors: Tihomir Urošević (R0800); Ana Kovačević (outside co-author).
Keywords: PIFA; LoRa antenna; 868 MHz; PCB antenna; radiation efficiency.
A compact planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) was designed and fabricated for integration onto a 50 mm × 30 mm PCB intended for battery-powered LoRa sensor nodes. The antenna occupies a 25 mm × 8 mm footprint on an FR-4 substrate with 1.6 mm thickness. Matching was achieved through a shorting strip and a tuning slot, yielding a measured −10 dB bandwidth of 28 MHz centred at 868 MHz, covering the full European LoRa band. Measured gain was −0.8 dBi in free space and dropped by 1.4 dB when the PCB was placed inside an ABS plastic enclosure of 2 mm wall thickness. Radiation efficiency was 61 %. The sensitivity of the resonant frequency to hand proximity was characterised using a phantom limb fixture; detuning of up to 14 MHz was observed, which remains within the matched bandwidth. The design is compared against a monopole reference and a commercially available chip antenna.

[SYN-PUB-06842] publication · Shielding Gas Composition Effects on Weld Bead Geometry and Spatter in MIG Welding of 1.0 mm DC01 Sheet at Low Heat Input · 2023 · researchers R0593
Shielding Gas Composition Effects on Weld Bead Geometry and Spatter in MIG Welding of 1.0 mm DC01 Sheet at Low Heat Input (2023, journal, International Journal of Welding Science and Practice).
Authors: Đuro Simić (R0593); Tamara Novković (outside co-author); Uroš Filipović (outside co-author).
Keywords: shielding gas; Ar/CO₂; thin sheet; heat input; bead geometry.
Very thin mild-steel sheet (1.0 mm DC01) presents a narrow operating window in MIG welding because heat input must be minimised to avoid burn-through while maintaining fusion. This paper reports the effect of Ar/CO₂ mixture ratios (75/25, 82/18, 90/10, and 97/3 vol%) on spatter mass, bead width, dilution, and distortion in bead-on-plate welds at a fixed heat input of 85 J/mm. Forty-eight specimens were welded and measured. Ar/CO₂ 90/10 produced the lowest spatter mass (0.06 g/m) and the most consistent bead width (coefficient of variation 4.2 %), while 75/25 produced 0.21 g/m spatter. Hardness traverses across the heat-affected zone showed a maximum of 198 HV1 for all gas compositions, indicating no detrimental microstructural change. Distortion, measured by three-point deflection, was lowest at 97/3 but accompanied by an irregular bead profile with 14 % of runs showing incomplete fusion. The 90/10 ratio is recommended as the practical optimum for this thickness.

Review the claims of pair C008-CH4:R1022.
It is about: researcher Milutin Paunović (R1022) and company Elekron Sistemi a.d. (C008), challenge C008-CH4.

Claims:
1. The challenge traces two field failures to race conditions in the interrupt layer of a bare-metal C firmware codebase and requires systematic detection without a rewrite (C008-CH4). [C008-CH4]
2. Paunović co-authored work on static analysis for data-race detection in interrupt-driven C firmware using lock-set analysis and GCC plugins (SYN-PUB-10581, SYN-PUB-10238). [SYN-PUB-10581, SYN-PUB-10238]
3. Paunović co-authored work on formal verification of interrupt-driven firmware using model checking in SPIN and Promela (SYN-PUB-10588, SYN-PUB-10586, SYN-PUB-10583). [SYN-PUB-10588, SYN-PUB-10586, SYN-PUB-10583]
4. Paunović collaborated with a Novi Sad-based automotive electronics supplier during SAFE-MIGRATE, providing refactoring support for a production motor-controller firmware codebase (SYN-PRJ-0383). [SYN-PRJ-0383]
5. The publications cover interrupt-driven firmware race detection; coverage of flash-write timing hazards specifically as a race-condition class is not stated in those records (SYN-PUB-10581, SYN-PUB-10238). [SYN-PUB-10581, SYN-PUB-10238]
6. The SAFE-MIGRATE collaboration covered a motor-controller codebase; whether that work scaled to a 340,000-line codebase comparable to the RTU firmware is not stated (SYN-PRJ-0383). [SYN-PRJ-0383]

Review the claims of profile R0842.
It is about: researcher Péter Szabó (R0842).

Claims:
1. Extreme-value theory and generalised Pareto distribution modelling for heavy-tailed risk data in small samples. [SYN-PUB-09112, SYN-PUB-09113, SYN-PUB-09110, R0842]
2. Bayesian hierarchical models for credibility-adjusted tail quantile estimation in heterogeneous risk groups. [SYN-PUB-09116, SYN-PUB-09112, SYN-PUB-09109]
3. Sequential Monte Carlo algorithms for updating catastrophe loss models with new extreme-event observations. [SYN-PUB-09115]
4. Sensitivity analysis and threshold selection methods for peaks-over-threshold modelling under model uncertainty. [SYN-PUB-08138, SYN-PUB-09110]
5. Prior elicitation protocols for Bayesian analysis of heavy-tailed distributions in non-life insurance and operational risk contexts. [SYN-PUB-09113, SYN-PUB-09111]
6. Ruin probability approximations for compound Poisson risk processes with Pareto claim severities. [SYN-PUB-09114]
7. Collective risk modelling and posterior predictive distributions for aggregate loss from sparse historical data. [SYN-PUB-09111]
8. Application and validation of extreme-value models to regional flood, agricultural, and motor insurance loss data. [SYN-PUB-06563, SYN-PUB-09116, SYN-PUB-08138]
9. Open to contract research on tail risk quantification and extreme-loss modelling, and consulting for insurance or reinsurance companies on Bayesian reserving and capital modelling. [R0842]
10. Open to supervision of industrial PhD candidates placed at NTP companies with actuarial or risk analytics activities. [R0842]
11. Led the statistical methodology work package of CATTOOL, an applied Bayesian modelling toolkit for underwriting and reserving deployed with two regional non-life insurers in Hungary and Serbia. [SYN-PRJ-0117]
12. Provided consultancy to a regional reinsurance brokerage in Novi Sad during 2018–2019 on internal model validation under Solvency II for non-life insurance. [R0842]

Review the claims of profile R0571.
It is about: researcher Mirjana Malešević (R0571).

Claims:
1. Automated schema-drift detection in event-driven data pipelines, using incremental probabilistic field tracking to distinguish transient field appearances from stable schema additions. [SYN-PUB-06622, SYN-PUB-06617]
2. Consistency validation across multiple API sources using event reconciliation, field-level comparison, and conflict detection for distributed systems. [SYN-PUB-06616]
3. Anomaly detection in high-frequency multivariate telemetry using unsupervised learning methods including Isolation Forest and one-class SVM on streaming data. [SYN-PUB-06618, SYN-PUB-06623]
4. Design patterns for embedding data quality checks into Apache Kafka-based pipelines, covering inline validators, side-car topics, quality-aware processors, and batch reconciliation. [SYN-PUB-06619]
5. Detection of silent data corruption caused by middleware caching in microservice architectures through consistency audit mechanisms comparing cached and uncached payloads. [SYN-PUB-06620]
6. Benchmarking and reproducible evaluation of schema-drift detection methods under controlled injection, comparing rule-based and statistical approaches on JSON API streams. [SYN-PUB-06621]
7. Rule-based REST API response validation and schema monitoring for detecting structural inconsistencies and undocumented schema changes in web service endpoints. [SYN-PUB-06614]
8. Led the APIGUARD project integrating data quality monitoring into API gateway infrastructure for small and medium enterprises, in partnership with the Vojvodina ICT Cluster. [SYN-PRJ-0115]
9. Principal investigator of DAQSTREAM, which conducted pilot deployments with industry partners in logistics and retail sectors and released open-source monitoring toolkit and evaluation datasets. [SYN-PRJ-0114]
10. Worked as a software engineer at a regional IT services company from 2014 to 2016 on integration projects connecting ERP systems via REST APIs. [R0571…[+19941 chars]

Review the claims of pair C004-CH3:R0842.
It is about: researcher Péter Szabó (R0842) and company OsiguroMi d.o.o. (C004), challenge C004-CH3.

Claims:
1. OsiguroMi's core difficulty is unstable loss curves from fewer than 200 historical events, and the company's actuarial team cannot complete this work on its own (C004-CH3). [C004-CH3]
2. Szabó's expertise covers extreme-value theory and generalised Pareto distribution modelling for heavy-tailed risk data specifically in small samples (SYN-PUB-09112, SYN-PUB-09113, SYN-PUB-09110). [SYN-PUB-09112, SYN-PUB-09113, SYN-PUB-09110]
3. Szabó's work includes Bayesian hierarchical models for credibility-adjusted tail quantile estimation in heterogeneous risk groups, and collective risk modelling with posterior predictive distributions for aggregate loss from sparse historical data (SYN-PUB-09116, SYN-PUB-09111). [SYN-PUB-09116, SYN-PUB-09111]
4. Szabó led the statistical methodology work package of CATTOOL, an applied Bayesian modelling toolkit for underwriting and reserving deployed with two regional non-life insurers in Hungary and Serbia (SYN-PRJ-0117). [SYN-PRJ-0117]
5. Szabó is open to contract research on tail risk quantification and extreme-loss modelling and consulting for insurance companies on Bayesian reserving (R0842). [R0842]
6. The publications cover flood, agricultural, and motor insurance loss data (SYN-PUB-06563, SYN-PUB-09116, SYN-PUB-08138); none is recorded as covering precipitation-triggered parametric event-cancellation insurance specifically. [SYN-PUB-06563, SYN-PUB-09116, SYN-PUB-08138]

Sources:
[C004-CH3] challenge · We want to price parametric festival-cancellation policies based on historical weather and event cancellation data, but we have fewer than 200 historical festival events in our database and standard actuarial methods need far more data points to produce stable loss curves. · company C004

It is about: researcher Jasmina Arsić (R0664) and company OsiguroMi d.o.o. (C004), challenge C004-CH3.

Claims:
1. OsiguroMi requires a methodology applicable to different locations in the region despite sparse event history (C004-CH3), and has access to RHMZS meteorological data (C004). [C004-CH3, C004]
2. Arsić's work includes regional frequency analysis using L-moments and Wasserstein barycenters to reduce estimation uncertainty for rare multivariate quantiles at ungauged locations (SYN-PUB-07511). [SYN-PUB-07511]
3. Arsić co-authored work on peaks-over-threshold modelling and threshold selection diagnostics for bivariate extremes, and on max-stable processes fitted by pairwise composite likelihood for spatial risk assessment of extreme precipitation (SYN-PUB-07506, SYN-PUB-03207). [SYN-PUB-07506, SYN-PUB-03207]
4. Arsić carried out a six-month consulting engagement developing copula-based aggregate loss models for weather-related claims portfolios in the Adriatic–Pannonian region (R0664). [R0664]
5. Arsić and OsiguroMi would apply regional frequency analysis and peaks-over-threshold copula methods to the company's festival-weather event database and RHMZS precipitation records, to reduce estimation uncertainty for rare precipitation quantiles across locations in the region and support stable parametric pricing (C004-CH3, C004), using methods from SYN-PUB-07511, SYN-PUB-07506, SYN-PUB-03207. [C004-CH3, C004, SYN-PUB-07511, SYN-PUB-07506, SYN-PUB-03207]

Arsić's recorded expertise covers the meteorological and multivariate extreme-value side; the publications cover environmental extremes (SYN-PUB-07512, SYN-PUB-07511, SYN-PUB-07507) rather than actuarial loss-curve construction or parametric insurance pricing specifically. 2. [C008-CH4, SYN-PUB-04582, SYN-PUB-04581, SYN-PUB-04586]

Sources:
[C008-CH4] challenge · The RTU firmware we ship has grown to 340,000 lines of C code over 20 years and nobody on the team fully understands the interrupt-handling layer anymore — we had two field failures in the last year caused by race conditions that took an average of 11 weeks each to reproduce and fix, which is unacceptable for critical infrastructure clients. · company C008
The RTU firmware we ship has grown to 340,000 lines of C code over 20 years and nobody on the team fully understands the interrupt-handling layer anymore — we had two field failures in the last year caused by race conditions that took an average of 11 weeks each to reproduce and fix, which is unacceptable for critical infrastructure clients.

Our main RTU firmware is a C codebase that has been added to by many different engineers since 2003. It now runs to about 340,000 lines and the interrupt-handling layer was written by two engineers who have since retired. We had two separate field failures last year — both traced back to race conditions where an interrupt fired during a flash-write operation and corrupted a register. Static Detection of Data Races in Interrupt-Driven C Firmware Using Lock-Set Analysis (2011, journal, Journal of Embedded Computing and Microelectronics).
Authors: Milutin Paunović (R1022); Dragan Vuković (outside co-author); Miroslav Šešlija (outside co-author).
Keywords: data race detection; lock-set analysis; interrupt-driven firmware; static analysis; GCC plugin.
Interrupt-driven firmware written in C is prone to data races that are difficult to expose through testing because race conditions depend on precise interrupt timing. This paper adapts the classical lock-set algorithm to the interrupt-preemption model used in bare-metal microcontroller firmware, where mutual exclusion is typically enforced by disabling specific interrupt vectors rather than by acquiring locks. The analysis is implemented as a GCC plugin and evaluated on six open-source firmware projects ranging from 8 kB to 120 kB of source code. Review the claims of profile R0571.
It is about: researcher Mirjana Malešević (R0571).

Claims:
1. Anomaly detection in high-frequency multivariate telemetry using unsupervised learning methods including Isolation Forest on streaming data. [SYN-PUB-06618]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-06618] publication · Applying Isolation Forest to Multivariate Numeric Anomalies in High-Frequency API Telemetry · 2021 · researchers R0571
Applying Isolation Forest to Multivariate Numeric Anomalies in High-Frequency API Telemetry (2021, conference, Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Data Quality in Engineering Systems (DQES 2021)).
Authors: Mirjana Malešević (R0571); Luka Todorović (outside co-author); Péter Kovács (outside co-author).
Keywords: Isolation Forest; multivariate anomaly detection; IoT telemetry; streaming data; unsupervised learning.
High-frequency telemetry streams produced by IoT gateways and industrial APIs exhibit multivariate numeric patterns that rule-based detectors handle poorly when anomalies involve correlated deviations across several fields simultaneously. This paper investigates the use of the Isolation Forest algorithm for unsupervised anomaly detection in such streams, focusing on tuning the contamination parameter and the number of estimators under streaming constraints. Experiments used telemetry data from a factory automation pilot comprising six sensor channels sampled at 10 Hz over 30 days, yielding approximately 15.5 million records. Isolation Forest outperformed a univariate z-score baseline by 18 percentage points in F1 score on held-out labelled anomaly windows. The paper also reports the effect of sub-sampling strategies on detection quality when full-stream processing is not feasible, and provides a reference configuration table for practitioners operating within defined memory budgets. No labelled training data was required beyond the held-out evaluation set.

Design of a Rainfall Deficit Index for Maize Insurance in the Vojvodina Region: Sensitivity to Spatial Resolution of Input Precipitation Grids (2020, journal, Journal of Agricultural Risk and Finance).
Authors: Ljubica Ristić (outside co-author); Nataša Filipović (outside co-author); Marco Ceriani (outside co-author); Žarko Pejić (R0364).
Keywords: rainfall deficit index; basis risk; maize insurance; CHIRPS; ERA5; DSSAT.
Index insurance products that trigger payouts based on area-average rainfall can suffer from basis risk when the spatial resolution of the underlying precipitation data does not capture field-level variability. This study quantified how the choice of precipitation grid resolution (0.25°, 0.05°, and 1 km downscaled) affects the properties of a 30-day rainfall deficit index (RDI) designed for rainfed maize in Vojvodina. Historical RDI series were reconstructed for 1995–2018 using ERA5 reanalysis at 0.25°, CHIRPS at 0.05°, and a KED-downscaled product at 1 km. Basis risk was approximated by computing the correlation between field-scale simulated crop water deficits from a DSSAT maize model and each RDI series for 120 sample parcels. SAFE-MIGRATE: Methodology and Tool Support for Safe Migration of Legacy Embedded C Code to MISRA-C:2012 (Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research, 2018–2020).
Participants: R1022 principal investigator.
Partners: NTP Novi Sad — tenant company Embeddium d.o.o.; Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad.
SAFE-MIGRATE developed practical methods and tool support to assist small and medium embedded-systems companies in the Vojvodina region in migrating legacy C firmware to MISRA-C:2012 compliance. The project produced the initial version of the MisraFix rewriting tool, a catalogue of refactoring patterns for safety-relevant firmware, and a training programme delivered to engineers at two local companies working on automotive and industrial control products. The project included a pilot application in which the methodology was applied to a 47 kB motor-controller firmware under an industry collaboration agreement. A total of four peer-reviewed publications resulted from the project.

A Semi-Supervised One-Class SVM Framework for Rare-Event Detection with Partial Label Information (2018, journal, Pattern Recognition and Data Analysis).
Authors: Olivera Rakić (R0071); Bojana Filipović (outside co-author); Tomáš Novotný (outside co-author).
Keywords: one-class SVM; semi-supervised learning; anomaly detection; partial labels; constraint optimisation.
In many industrial monitoring scenarios, operators can label a small fraction of anomalous events while the majority of the data stream remains unlabelled. Standard one-class SVM (OC-SVM) ignores partial labels entirely; this paper proposes a constrained OC-SVM variant that incorporates labelled anomalies as must-outside constraints during kernel optimisation. The method is evaluated on four datasets: bearing degradation signals, network intrusion logs, medical ECG records with annotated arrhythmia bursts, and a synthetic benchmark with controlled sparsity of positive labels (1%, 5%, 10%, 20%). At 5% label density, the constrained OC-SVM reduces false-negative rate by 18 percentage points relative to the unconstrained baseline without statistically significant change in false-positive rate. Review the claims of profile R0364.
It is about: researcher Žarko Pejić (R0364).

Claims:
1. Analysis of a dense disdrometer transect to characterise sub-kilometre spatial coherence and decorrelation of convective rainfall intensity. [SYN-PUB-04466]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-04466] publication · Assessing sub-kilometre spatial coherence of convective rainfall using a dense disdrometer transect across the Fruška Gora ridge · 2024 · researchers R0700, R0388, R0364
Assessing sub-kilometre spatial coherence of convective rainfall using a dense disdrometer transect across the Fruška Gora ridge (2024, journal, Quarterly Journal of Hydrometeorology).
Authors: Дарко Тошић (R0700); Тамара Јовановић (outside co-author); Luca Ferretti (outside co-author); Srđan Ognjanov (R0388); Žarko Pejić (R0364).
Keywords: spatial coherence; disdrometer transect; Fruška Gora; convective rainfall; decorrelation length.
A transect of 22 optical disdrometers spaced 800 m apart along a 17.5 km line perpendicular to the Fruška Gora mountain ridge was operated during May–September 2022 to characterise the spatial decorrelation of convective rainfall intensity at sub-kilometre scales. During 38 convective events, inter-instrument correlation coefficients for 5-minute intensities were computed as a function of separation distance and storm advection direction. The correlation length for 5-minute intensities exceeded 8 km for stratiform rainfall but dropped to 2.1 km for intense convective cells (R > 20 mm h⁻¹). An anisotropy ratio of 1.6 was identified between the ridge-parallel and ridge-perpendicular directions, attributable to orographic forcing of cell alignment. These results impose quantitative limits on the validity of spatial interpolation at spacings used by most national rain-gauge networks. Implications for the accuracy of kriging-merged products at sub-hourly time steps are discussed with reference to the error budgets reported in our earlier Pannonian Plain merging study.

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-00960] publication · A Semi-Supervised One-Class SVM Framework for Rare-Event Detection with Partial Label Information · 2018 · researchers R0071
A Semi-Supervised One-Class SVM Framework for Rare-Event Detection with Partial Label Information (2018, journal, Pattern Recognition and Data Analysis).
Authors: Olivera Rakić (R0071); Bojana Filipović (outside co-author); Tomáš Novotný (outside co-author).
Keywords: one-class SVM; semi-supervised learning; anomaly detection; partial labels; constraint optimisation.
In many industrial monitoring scenarios, operators can label a small fraction of anomalous events while the majority of the data stream remains unlabelled. Standard one-class SVM (OC-SVM) ignores partial labels entirely; this paper proposes a constrained OC-SVM variant that incorporates labelled anomalies as must-outside constraints during kernel optimisation. The method is evaluated on four datasets: bearing degradation signals, network intrusion logs, medical ECG records with annotated arrhythmia bursts, and a synthetic benchmark with controlled sparsity of positive labels (1%, 5%, 10%, 20%). At 5% label density, the constrained OC-SVM reduces false-negative rate by 18 percentage points relative to the unconstrained baseline without statistically significant change in false-positive rate. The framework adds a single hyperparameter controlling constraint weight and remains tractable for datasets up to 500,000 samples with an RBF kernel. Ablation studies confirm that gains diminish beyond 15% label density, at which point a supervised SVM becomes preferable.

Review the claims of profile R0727.
It is about: researcher Milutin Đukić (R0727).

Claims:
1. Canopy temperature estimation at 10 m resolution by kriging with external drift using Sentinel-2 red-edge reflectance bands (705 nm and 740 nm) combined with field-level thermal measurements for crop water stress assessment. [SYN-PUB-04706]

Sources:
[SYN-PUB-04706] publication · Sentinel-2 Red-Edge Bands as Auxiliary Variables for Spatial Interpolation of Canopy Temperature: A Case Study in Sunflower Fields of Vojvodina · 2019 · researchers R0480, R0727, R0388
Sentinel-2 Red-Edge Bands as Auxiliary Variables for Spatial Interpolation of Canopy Temperature: A Case Study in Sunflower Fields of Vojvodina (2019, journal, Remote Sensing of Environment and Precision Crop Science).
Authors: Nataša Brkić (outside co-author); Goran Filipović (outside co-author); Anna Turčanová (R0480); Milutin Đukić (R0727); Srđan Ognjanov (R0388).
Keywords: Sentinel-2; red-edge; canopy temperature; kriging with external drift; sunflower.
Thermal infrared sensors aboard Landsat-8 and Sentinel-3 provide land surface temperature at resolutions too coarse for field-scale crop stress assessment. This study tested whether Sentinel-2 red-edge and near-infrared reflectance bands, sampled in July–August 2017 during cloud-free overpasses over 4 200 ha of commercial sunflower in Vojvodina, could serve as auxiliary predictors in a kriging-with-external-drift model for canopy temperature. Canopy temperature was measured with 22 handheld infrared thermometers installed at 10-minute intervals across three farms. KED using a linear combination of the 705 nm and 740 nm Sentinel-2 bands reduced interpolation RMSE from 1.8 °C (OK) to 1.1 °C at 10 m resolution, a 39 % improvement. Spatial maps produced daily from the KED surface correlated with manually scouted water-stress incidence zones at r = 0.74. The method requires no additional satellite acquisitions beyond the freely available Sentinel-2 archive.

Review the claims of proposal C004-CH1-R0727.
It is about: researcher Milutin Đukić (R0727) and company OsiguroMi d.o.o. (C004), challenge C004-CH1.

Claims:
1. OsiguroMi d.o.o. works in insurtech — embedded micro-insurance and parametric products. [C004]
2. Milutin Đukić is a Principal Research Fellow in the Remote Sensing and GIS Group, BioSense Institute. [R0727]
3. OsiguroMi's parametric crop insurance pays out when the nearest official station records rainfall below a contracted threshold, but that station is sometimes 30 km from the insured plot and separated from it by terrain features that substantially alter local rainfall. [C004-CH1]
4. Partners in Vojvodina and Bačka report that payouts were triggered when fields had not dried out, and were withheld when crops had already been lost — direct evidence of basis risk. [C004-CH1]
5. The company has access to RHMZS data and three private agrometeorological networks totalling around 140 measurement points in the region, and has considered satellite soil-moisture indices, but is uncertain how to combine these sources into a single reliable trigger. [C004-CH1]
6. OsiguroMi plans to expand the agro line to Bulgaria and Romania by the end of 2025, making a scalable and reproducible spatial estimation method strategically important. [C004]
7. A 2021 study reports that ordinary co-kriging incorporating SMOS satellite-derived soil moisture alongside rain-gauge station data improves spatial interpolation of quarterly and monthly precipitation compared with ordinary kriging alone. [W3137160051]
8. A 2022 study reports that an optimised kriging approach interpolating relative rainfall anomalies at 250 m resolution over a 30-year record achieves R² = 0.78 in leave-one-out cross-validation against 622 stations, though with a known smoothing effect at high-rainfall extremes. [W4213059839]

claim.text: Tihomir Urošević co-authored work on path-loss modelling and link-budget prediction for indoor and industrial LoRaWAN deployments using empirical measurement data.

rejected.reason: critic: SYN-PUB-08743 covers a link-budget tool for LoRaWAN deployments using empirical measurement data, and SYN-PUB-06790 covers penetration loss measurements — not 'path-loss modelling and link-budget prediction for indoor and industrial LoRaWAN deployments'; SYN-PUB-06790 is about greenhouse structures, not indoor/industrial LoRaWAN deployments, so the claim incorrectly attributes path-loss modelling for indoor/industrial LoRaWAN to SYN-PUB-06790.

claim.text: The company's collar devices lose approximately 9% of daily readings at SF12 in reinforced concrete basements, with SLA penalties running, and fixed-price contracts bar replacing gateways or re-running cables.

rejected.reason: critic-2: 26% likely that the cited text supports it.

claim.text: Urošević co-authored work on path-loss modelling for indoor LoRaWAN deployments and on compact 868 MHz PIFA design for LoRa — the two technical axes the fix requires.

rejected.reason: critic: The claim adds the editorial judgement 'the two technical axes the fix requires', which is a characterisation of how the records relate to the company's problem and is not stated in either SYN-PUB-08743 or SYN-PUB-08741.

claim.text: The propagation-through-materials work covers greenhouse structures and hospital buildings; the records do not cover reinforced concrete basement characterization at the depth and wall thickness typical of municipal meter rooms (SYN-PUB-06790, SYN-PUB-08744).

rejected.reason: critic: SYN-PUB-06790 covers greenhouse structures and SYN-PUB-08744 covers hospital buildings, but the claim adds the editorial judgement that these records 'do not cover reinforced concrete basement characterization at the depth and wall thickness typical of municipal meter rooms', which is an inference about scope not stated in either cited record.

claim.text: SYN-PUB-08743 covers link-budget prediction and SYN-PUB-08741 covers compact antenna design; neither record covers adaptive spreading-factor control or packet-recovery algorithms.

rejected.reason: critic: The claim that 'neither record covers adaptive spreading-factor control or packet-recovery algorithms' is an absence-of-content assertion about the cited records, which goes beyond what a record states — SYN-PUB-08743 does cover spreading-factor assignments per zone, so the claim that it does not cover adaptive spreading-factor control is also factually incorrect based on the cited text.

claim.text: The company transfers six months of per-device RSSI, SNR, and packet-delivery logs from all three municipal sites to the researcher's group under a signed data-use agreement; the researcher reviews them to prioritise the worst-performing meter rooms for measurement.

rejected.reason: C008-CH1 mentions only RSSI values and packet-delivery rates as tracked metrics; neither C008-CH1 nor any other source states that the company holds per-device SNR logs, so SNR logs are presented as existing company data without support.

claim.text: the company has a live, penalty-bearing signal problem in a specific physical environment it cannot solve with configuration changes alone, but it lacks the propagation measurement tools and antenna design expertise to diagnose and fix it within the project window.

rejected.reason: The claim that the company lacks propagation measurement tools and antenna design expertise is a stated limitation of the company not found in C008, C008-CH1, or any other cited source, which say only that standard configuration tuning has been exhausted (claim 5) and list the company's four engineers and lab equipment without characterising any gap in measurement or design capability.

claim.text: The researcher brings the exact combination needed — indoor path-loss measurement methods, sub-GHz antenna design for LoRa collar form factors, and prior LoRaWAN link-budget validation on a live project — but has no access to production meter rooms or the deployment data needed to calibrate a real-world model.

rejected.reason: The statement that the researcher has no access to production meter rooms or deployment data is a stated limitation of the researcher not found in R0800 or any other cited source.

Review the claims of proposal C008-CH1-R0800.
It is about: researcher Tihomir Urošević (R0800) and company Elekron Sistemi a.d. (C008), challenge C008-CH1.

Claims:
1. Repositioning gateway antennas and adding a repeater node brought limited improvement; the ReachRate applied research project must deliver a solution within 14 months. [C008-CH1, C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Receives Provincial Innovation Fund Grant for LoRaWAN Signal Research]
2. Three live municipal utility deployments in Bosnia and North Macedonia with real basement meter rooms are available for field testing. [C008-CH1, C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Receives Provincial Innovation Fund Grant for LoRaWAN Signal Research]
3. A senior RF engineer who led the original LoRaWAN collar development serves as project lead for ReachRate. [C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Receives Provincial Innovation Fund Grant for LoRaWAN Signal Research]
4. Urošević co-authored work on a link-budget tool for LoRaWAN deployments using empirical measurement data. [SYN-PUB-08743]
5. The company's collar devices receive at -120 to -125 dBm in basement meter rooms, losing approximately 9% of daily readings at SF12, under fixed-price municipal contracts that bar replacing gateways or re-running cables. [C008-CH1]
6. Urošević co-authored work on a link-budget tool for LoRaWAN deployments and on compact planar inverted-F antenna design for 868 MHz LoRa integration. [SYN-PUB-08743, SYN-PUB-08741]
7. The propagation-through-materials work covers greenhouse structures and hospital buildings. [SYN-PUB-06790, SYN-PUB-08744]

Sources:
[C008-CH1] challenge · We are retrofitting legacy water and heat meters for three municipal clients in Bosnia and North Macedonia with our LoRaWAN collar device, but the received signal strength inside basement meter rooms is between -120 and -125 dBm, which is at the edge of our gateway sensitivity — about 9% of readings are missing per day and the clients are threatening penalty claus…[+9470 chars]

Review the free text of proposal C008-CH1-R0800.
It is about: researcher Tihomir Urošević (R0800) and company Elekron Sistemi a.d. (C008), challenge C008-CH1.

The claims are checked one by one elsewhere: take them as given. In the proposal each one shows as ⟨claim N⟩.
Check only the other text: the research questions, approach, plan, first steps, the reasoning under "Why this pair" and
the terms agreed up front.

Free text may propose new work and new data ("collect", "label", "set up", "measure", "aim for"), and may reason from the
claims. List a sentence only when it:
- presents as already true a fact about the company or the researcher (data, recordings, a dataset size, history,
  equipment, staff, a skill, what a method does, a past result) that neither the claims nor the sources state;
- works on data the company is not shown to have: for every archive, dataset, log, set of past scans or recordings the
  plan uses as existing, find the claim or source that says the company has it, with the properties the text gives it
  (size, period, format, the device it comes from, its labels). Data the plan says it will collect is fine;
- says what a side lacks or cannot do, and the claims and sources do not say so, or say the opposite;
- contradicts a claim or a source;
- plans work that breaks a limit the company states (a rate it may not go below, hardware it cannot change).
Quote each such sentence whole, exactly as written. Give one reason per sentence and name the claim or source it rests on.
Return an empty list when the free text is fine.

Claims:
1. Elekron Sistemi a.d. works in ioT and electronics hardware. [C008]
2. Tihomir Urošević is a Research Associate in the Department of Power, Electronics and Telecommunications, Faculty of Technical Sciences. [R0800]
3. LoRaWAN collar devices on water and heat meters in basement meter rooms at three municipal clients receive at -120 to -125 dBm, at gateway sensitivity, losing approximately 9% of daily readings even at SF1…[+30996 chars]

Review the claims of proposal C004-CH1-R0727.
It is about: researcher Milutin Đukić (R0727) and company OsiguroMi d.o.o. (C004), challenge C004-CH1.

Claims:
1. OsiguroMi plans to expand the agro line to Bulgaria and Romania by the end of 2025 through partnerships with regional cooperatives. [C004]
2. A 2021 study assessed ordinary kriging (OK) and ordinary cokriging (OCK) for spatial interpolation of quarterly and monthly precipitation in Poland, incorporating SMOS satellite-derived soil moisture data alongside rain-gauge station data. [W3137160051]
3. PostgreSQL databases with time series for historical losses, and partner feedback from Vojvodina and Bačka on cases where payouts were triggered without crop loss and withheld when crops were lost. [C004, C004-CH1]
4. An automated rules-based claims processing engine that pays out parametric triggers without requiring a claim request from the user. [C004]
5. Đukić is open to providing equipment and data infrastructure access for external researchers requiring Copernicus-based processing. [R0727]
6. OsiguroMi has a ~140-point mixed gauge network, satellite soil-moisture indices it has considered, and PostgreSQL time series for historical losses alongside partner feedback from Vojvodina and Bačka on payout accuracy. [C004-CH1, C004]
7. Đukić has published on co-kriging of precipitation with auxiliary co-variables and on wet-day indicator kriging for binary precipitation mapping. [SYN-PUB-08096, SYN-PUB-08093, SYN-PUB-08102]
8. Đukić is open to joint projects with agri-tech companies needing high-resolution climate data products and to MSc student internships in remote sensing data processing. [R0727]

the terms agreed up front.

Free text may propose new work and new data ("collect", "label", "set up", "measure", "aim for"), and may reason from the

Review the claims of proposal C008-CH1-R0800.
It is about: researcher Tihomir Urošević (R0800) and company Elekron Sistemi a.d. (C008), challenge C008-CH1.

Claims:
1. The company's collar devices receive at -120 to -125 dBm in basement meter rooms, losing approximately 9% of daily readings at SF12; fixed-price municipal contracts mean the company does not have budget for a full gateway infrastructure overhaul. [C008-CH1]

Sources:
[C008-CH1] challenge · We are retrofitting legacy water and heat meters for three municipal clients in Bosnia and North Macedonia with our LoRaWAN collar device, but the received signal strength inside basement meter rooms is between -120 and -125 dBm, which is at the edge of our gateway sensitivity — about 9% of readings are missing per day and the clients are threatening penalty clauses after six months of missed SLA. · company C008
We are retrofitting legacy water and heat meters for three municipal clients in Bosnia and North Macedonia with our LoRaWAN collar device, but the received signal strength inside basement meter rooms is between -120 and -125 dBm, which is at the edge of our gateway sensitivity — about 9% of readings are missing per day and the clients are threatening penalty clauses after six months of missed SLA.

We are fitting our LoRaWAN collar device onto existing water and heat meters in basement plant rooms for three municipal clients — two in Bosnia and one in North Macedonia. The problem is signal. Measured RSSI inside these rooms runs between -120 and -125 dBm, right at the edge of what our gateways can reliably decode. We are using SF12 already, which is the slowest spreading factor and gives us the best link budget, but we are still losing around 9% of daily readings. The SLA we signed requires 99% daily read success, so we are in breach and have been for six months. Review the free text of proposal C008-CH1-R0800.
It is about: researcher Tihomir Urošević (R0800) and company Elekron Sistemi a.d. (C008), challenge C008-CH1.

The claims are checked one by one elsewhere: take them as given. In the proposal each one shows as ⟨claim N⟩.
Check only the other text: the research questions, approach, plan, first steps, the reasoning under "Why this pair" and
the terms agreed up front.

Free text may propose new work and new data ("collect", "label", "set up", "measure", "aim for"), and may reason from the
claims. List a sentence only when it:
- presents as already true a fact about the company or the researcher (data, recordings, a dataset size, history,

Return an empty list when the free text is fine.

Review the claims of proposal C004-CH1-R0727.
It is about: researcher Milutin Đukić (R0727) and company OsiguroMi d.o.o. (C004), challenge C004-CH1.

Claims:
1. An automated rules-based claims processing engine, and parametric triggers that pay out without requiring a claim request from the user. [C004]
2. OsiguroMi has RHMZS data and data from three private agrometeorological networks totalling around 140 measurement points, satellite soil-moisture indices it has considered, PostgreSQL time series for historical losses, and partner feedback from Vojvodina and Bačka on cases where payouts were triggered without crop loss and withheld when crops were lost. [C004-CH1, C004]

Sources:
[C004] company · OsiguroMi d.o.o. · 2019 · company C004
OsiguroMi d.o.o. (C004): Insurtech — embedded micro-insurance and parametric products, Novi Sad, 58 employees, founded 2019.
OsiguroMi d.o.o. je insurtech kompanija iz Novog Sada, osnovana 2019. godine sa jednom idejom: da osiguranje prestane da bude papirologija i postane tihi servis ugrađen u alate koje ljudi već koriste. Umesto da korisnik kupuje polisu na posebnom sajtu, naša tehnologija se integriše direktno u aplikacije za rezervaciju putovanja, agro-platforme i prodajne sisteme organizatora festivala — i polisa nastaje u trenutku transakcije. Radimo sa B2B partnerima širom Srbije i EU: putničkim platformama, zadrugama, organizatorima open-air događaja. Naš tim od 58 zaposlenih dolazi iz osiguranja, softverskog inženjerstva i analize podataka. Osnivači Milena Čabarkapa i Dragan Horvat prethodno su radili u reosiguranju i fintech sektoru, što je oblikovalo naš pristup: prvo model, pa produkt. Ono što nas razlikuje nije marketing — razlikuje nas API koji se može uključiti za manje od jednog radnog dana i parametarski okidači koji ne zahtevaju korisnikov zahtev za naknadu.
